### 1. P2 — An ordinary killed restore's recorded partial stage becomes an unrecorded archived artifact

Sources: [archive traversal, lines 1512–1536](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/754e72714b77870db50224ee7da6f8eb847374e1/packages/coding-agent/src/cli/gc-cli.ts#L1512-L1536), [reclaim removal, lines 1904–1917](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/754e72714b77870db50224ee7da6f8eb847374e1/packages/coding-agent/src/cli/gc-cli.ts#L1904-L1917), and [record matching, lines 1498–1507](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/754e72714b77870db50224ee7da6f8eb847374e1/packages/coding-agent/src/session/session-archive.ts#L1498-L1507).

Fresh, real-CLI sequence:

1. Archive and reclaim: **0/0**.
2. Kill restore after its first artifact write: **-9**. Its live staging directory holds **65,536 of 2,097,152 bytes**, with a genuine, intact ledger record.
3. Retry restore: **0**, full genuine artifact restored, but the partial stage remains in the live artifact tree. No move instruction is printed.
4. Age the transcript to make the ordinary archive eligible, then archive: **0**. It copies the recorded live stage into the archive as an ordinary directory, while reporting the original live directory in `stagingResidue`.
5. Reclaim: **0**. It removes the original recorded live staging directory. **The ledger record still exists.**
6. Restore: **0**, `artifactsRestored:true`, `errors:[]`. The archived partial stage returns to the live tree. The record still points at the old live inode, not the archived copy.

No record was removed or forged, no writer raced the commands, and no quarantine command was used. The complete transcript and genuine artifact remain exact: this is false classification/completion and a contradiction of the retained-stage contract, **not a claim that the real artifact's only copy was deleted**. The body and changelog's lost-record exception does not describe this sequence: its record is present throughout.

I ran the same witness on `100c3b81`; its summary is identical. This is a previously unreported defect of the retained feature, **not a regression introduced by the split**. Address the recorded-live-stage path through archive/reclaim; do not treat the duplicate as an ordinary artifact merely because the ledger names its live source. No quarantine implementation is required to correct that behavior.

Evidence: `restore-stage-lifecycle.json`, `restore-stage-lifecycle-summary.json`, and `baseline-lifecycle/restore-stage-lifecycle-summary.json`.

## 2 (blocking) a FIFO at the same name hangs `gc --restore --apply` forever, holding the gc lock

## 3 (blocking) the residue ledger guards archive→live only: a killed `gc --restore` leaves a partial file that is then archived, reclaimed over and restored as a session artifact

`attacks.py` (`killed-restore-*`), `battery3.py` (`wedge-clean`), `battery4.py`
(`wedge-detail`), `battery5.py` (`wedge-absorbed`).

A real `gc --restore --apply` SIGKILLed while staging (`write-after`, `link-before`,
`link-after`) leaves `sessions/b/<id>/.a.<hex>.tmp/a` — 65,536 bytes of a partial copy —
and its ledger record.

- `gc --restore --apply` again: **exit 0**, artifacts restored, the live stage left in place,
  **no message at all** about it (`adviceEverPrinted: false`). The five-step recovery is
  only ever produced for residue under the *archive* artifact root
  (`copyTreeDereferenced` / `artifactRestoreConflicts` both pass `archiveArtifacts` to
  `stagingResidueUnder`), and a restore only ever stages into the *live* tree. So no
  restore residue can ever produce the message.
- `gc --reclaim --apply --forward-only`: **exit 1**, forever, with
  `…/.a.<hex>.tmp/a is not an independent archived copy of …` — nothing says "staging",
  nothing says what to do. Removing the directory by hand is the only fix and the product
  never says so: `reclaimBefore` 1 → hand-removal → `reclaimAfterHandRemoval` **0**,
  `restoreAfter` **0**, artifact exact (`wedge-detail`).
- Left alone until the session is cold again, `gc --archive --apply` **absorbs it**:
  `archived: 1`, exit 0, the 65,536-byte partial now at
  `archive/sessions/b/<id>/.a.<hex>.tmp` as an ordinary artifact, while still being listed
  under `stagingResidue` for the live copy. `reclaim` then exits 0 and deletes the live tree,
  and `restore` exits 0 and brings the partial home again (`wedge-absorbed`). The archive
  walk never consults the ledger.

The changelog (line 30) says "A staging directory a killed `gc --archive` **or `gc --restore`**
left … The restore's message for such a directory gives the recovery a review ran". For the
`gc --restore` half that is false: there is no message and no recovery.

### 2. P2 — The copyable command can move the stage into an archive tree through an existing destination symlink

Source: [the generated command, lines 1522–1534](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/754e72714b77870db50224ee7da6f8eb847374e1/packages/coding-agent/src/session/session-archive.ts#L1522-L1534). The new test checks lexical `path.relative`, not resolved containment, at [lines 3921–3923](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/754e72714b77870db50224ee7da6f8eb847374e1/packages/coding-agent/test/session-archive.test.ts#L3921-L3923).

After a genuine killed archive, I made `<agentDir>/gc-quarantine` a symlink to that session's archived artifact directory **before requesting the advice**. There was no concurrent writer. Restore refused **1**, as expected. I copied its exact command: `mkdir -p` followed the existing symlink; the fresh per-record `mkdir` succeeded; both moves returned **0**. Restore then returned **0** and copied the relocated partial stage and moved record into the live artifact tree. `archiveResidueCopiedLive:true` in `direct.jsonl`, case `inside-alias`.

This requires a pre-existing filesystem alias; it is not the default layout. But it directly contradicts the command's stated example of moving outside both trees. The second `mkdir` protects against an occupied leaf, not against an aliased parent. The advice must make the resolved destination check an explicit, executable part of the procedure, or supply a destination it has checked. Do not restore the removed automatic quarantine merely to fix this instruction.

No original artifact was overwritten in this case. The failure is that following the supplied command reports a successful restore with partial staging bytes published as artifacts.

**0** and carries the partial file home to
`sessions/b/<id>/rec0/.a.0123456789abcdef.tmp/a`.

The command that was removed from this pull request refused exactly this; its test
("quarantine refuses a destination that resolves into a session tree, and moves nothing")
is one of the 32 deleted. `mkdir -p` on an existing symlink-to-directory succeeds, so the
